scenario_description:
Objective: Keep tonight’s studio test-tile firing from becoming a preventable ventilation hazard during gusty weather.
Emerging Need: A routine firing, wind notice, then vent-flap reversal and odor shift the situation from ordinary monitoring to a time-sensitive ventilation concern.
Decision Context: Stored studio ventilation notes and trade contact records determine which symptom pattern matters, the appropriate non-structural service route, and the cutoff-relevant details.
Consequence: After the route closes, no injury or equipment damage is documented, but the firing remains scheduled without the intended pre-firing draft assurance.

parameter.title: Studio test-tile firing
parameter.description: Small underglaze test tiles in the detached studio; downdraft vent normally runs through heat-up and cooldown.

parameter.subject: Canyon wind advisory for this afternoon
parameter.body: East canyon winds are expected to gust 35-45 mph in central Santa Fe from 15:00 through late evening. Lightweight outdoor items and exhaust terminations may rattle during the advisory period.

parameter.content: While finishing the studio shelf cleanout, the kiln downdraft cap thumped inward twice during gusts and I caught a faint hot-metal smell by the kiln. I shut the studio door when I left; the CO alarm was quiet and I didn’t see smoke.

parameter.subject: Today’s Santa Fe kiln-vent route
parameter.body: A technician is already in Santa Fe this afternoon and one pre-firing vent check slot remains. Written route additions received by 14:30 Mountain can still be assigned today; later requests roll to Monday.

parameter.subject: Santa Fe route additions closed
parameter.body: Today’s pre-firing check board is now closed. No additional Santa Fe vent stops will be added before this evening.
